verdicts.reason: A keeps a clean centred stack (logo → kicker → one-line headline → body → CTA → legal) with clear hierarchy. But the card bleeds off the left, right and bottom edges, so it no longer reads as a framed card, and the book cover cuts awkwardly into the card's top edge. The legal line also sits cramped near the bottom. B shrinks the Inkwell & Lantern logo to an illegible thumbnail stuck in the card's top-left corner, so the brand is effectively lost. It also scatters body copy, CTA and tiny unreadable legal text into an unbalanced three-column row, and the kicker is offset right while the headline is centred.
